sources.evidence: Linux prerequisites, official TLS-verified installer command, prompts and login flow.
Bootstrap script was read, never executed; downloads and checks release-package SHA-256. Script provenance is not independently verified.
Source deployment, credentials, RustFS ownership, public URL, automatic HTTPS, migrations.
Authoritative mounts ./data/postgres, ./data/rustfs, ./data/runtime and ./data/license; acme is a named volume.
Default environment variable names and placeholders.
Consolidated migration history and version-specific upgrade constraints.
pg_dump custom-format database export; cluster-wide roles require separate handling.
Compose down -v removes named volumes, while bind mounts are host paths.

corrections: Previous self-hosting copy called runtime a persistent volume. The pinned Compose definition binds ./data/runtime; README prose misleadingly says down -v deletes that identity. The actual bind mount governs deletion.
Previous instructions omitted RustFS access and secret keys and directory permissions required for first startup.
Database alone is not a complete backup: object data, runtime identity, license state and optional ACME state may be needed.
limitations: Source deployment paths and example are pinned to the listed upstream revision; installer release contents may differ.
Installer and deployment commands were inspected, not executed against production.
No universal upgrade path or independent signature verification is asserted.

Database export applies only when MONKEYAI_DATABASE_URL is not overridden to another database; external PostgreSQL or S3 endpoints require their own coordinated backups. Keep db running for pg_dump and stop all application/object writers through the consistent backup window.

The downloaded bootstrap begins with #!/bin/sh, explicitly instructs sudo sh on non-root invocation, and invokes the packaged install.sh with sh. The official tutorial invokes the same bootstrap with bash; its POSIX shell entrypoint also supports the documented sudo sh sequence.
